topic: A's on-site refit vs B's session-masked coefficients, same gated session protocol

A_refit.fit: 512 taps fitted on 6 fresh segments of the current on-site H

B_masked.note: B published file sha 2c971a33...; the Q20 payload matches exactly e353c10e..., the file hash differs only by serialisation

protocol: external source off; before every trial a fixed -20 dBFS tone is played with the loop open and the trial is skipped unless the microphone settles within 1.5 dB of the session baseline (baseline taken after 8 s settle, last 3 gates within 1.2 dB)

B_masked.-9 dB: howled, main 405 Hz, mic -23.8 dBFS at the rail

b_prediction.measured: B's model howls already at -9 dB and there the limiting point is 405 Hz, so the predicted low-frequency limit is real, but the predicted +6.74 dB is not realised on this fixture

delay.warning: a 1 kHz tone cannot measure the delay: correlation peaks repeat every ~48.8 samples, so tones reported 70/118/21 - all the same true delay modulo the tone period. Only the white-noise figure is usable.

trap_found: with a drift-checked gate the same A_refit model that had 'held at 0 dB' in an earlier session now howls at -3 dB, so the fixture sits within about 1-2 dB of its boundary and single-session 'held' results must not be quoted as margins
verdict: B's session correction is worse than A's on-site refit on this fixture: it howls at -9 dB where the refit holds. The limiting band moves between 8.35 kHz and about 400 Hz depending on the model. Refit from the npz is the indicated next step.
